partners.mechanism_chain: THSD1 (HGNC:24124) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular Matrix Assembly and Organization (REACT:R-HSA-168772); Extracellular Matrix Assembly and Organization (REACT:R-HSA-168772) —LEADS_TO→ Ectopia lentis (HP:0001692); Extracellular Matrix Assembly and Organization (REACT:R-HSA-168772) —LEADS_TO→ Lymphatic malformation (HP:0030125); ADAMTSL4 (HGNC:29771) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular Matrix Assembly and Organization (REACT:R-HSA-168772). Loss-of-function mutations in THSD1 disrupt the normal assembly and organization of the extracellular matrix (ECM). This disruption affects the structural integrity of the lens zonules, leading to ectopia lentis. Concurrently, compromised ECM organization impacts lymphatic endothelial cell function and lymphatic vessel development, resulting in lymphatic malformations. While THSD1 is the primary focus for both diseases, ADAMTSL4, also implicated in ectopia lentis, is known to influence ECM processes, potentially converging on similar downstream pathways related to matrix integrity.

partners.mechanism_chain: ADAMTSL4 (HGNC:25952) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Ectopia lentis (HP:0001741); ADAMTS13 (HGNC:230) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombocytopenia (HP:0001874); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (HP:0001898). Mutations in ADAMTSL4 disrupt extracellular matrix organization leading to ectopia lentis. Similarly, mutations in ADAMTS13, which also plays a role in extracellular matrix homeostasis (specifically in regulating von Willebrand factor), disrupt this process, leading to microangiopathic hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia, hallmarks of TTP. The convergence is on the broader pathway of extracellular matrix organization, which is essential for both ocular lens integrity and vascular health.

### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. ectopia lentis et pupillae  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.727)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5083635, Reactome:R-HSA-5173214)

**Proposed mechanism:** ADAMTSL4 (HGNC:19706) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Ectopia lentis (HP:0000534); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Ectopia pupillae (HP:0007772). Loss-of-function mutations in ADAMTSL4 disrupt extracellular matrix organization, which is critical for lens and iris development, leading to the phenotypes of ectopia lentis and ectopia pupillae.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in ADAMTSL4 with a gain-of-function mechanism or variants in entirely different genes for one of the diseases would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs743153797)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of ADAMTSL4 in extracellular matrix organization provides a common target for potential therapeutic interventions aimed at stabilizing the lens and iris structures in both conditions.

#### 2. Weill-Marchesani syndrome 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.416)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5083635, Reactome:R-HSA-5173214)

**Proposed mechanism:** ADAMTS10 (HGNC:27060) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); ADAMTS10 (HGNC:27060) —DISRUPTS→ Connective tissue development (GO:0007474); ADAMTSL4 (HGNC:33934) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); ADAMTSL4 (HGNC:33934) —DISRUPTS→ Connective tissue development (GO:0007474); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Ectopia lentis (HP:0001701); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Brachydactyly (HP:0009770); Connective tissue development (GO:0007474) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004325); Connective tissue development (GO:0007474) —LEADS_TO→ Glaucoma (HP:0000501). Loss-of-function mutations in ADAMTS10 and ADAMTSL4 disrupt the organization of the extracellular matrix and connective tissue development, leading to the phenotypes of ectopia lentis (disease A), and brachydactyly, short stature, and glaucoma (disease B).

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in ADAMTS10 or ADAMTSL4 with predicted gain-of-function effects or variants in other genes entirely unrelated to extracellular matrix or connective tissue pathways would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Any pathogenic variant in ADAMTS10 or ADAMTSL4 with a gnomAD allele frequency > 0.001)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathways of extracellular matrix organization and connective tissue development affected by these genes could lead to novel therapeutic strategies for both conditions, potentially targeting matrix remodeling or stabilization.

#### 3. properdin deficiency, X-linked  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.385)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5083635, Reactome:R-HSA-5173214)

**Proposed mechanism:** ADAMTSL4 (HGNC:29611) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (REACT:R-HSA-168744); Extracellular matrix organization (REACT:R-HSA-168744) —LEADS_TO→ Ectopia lentis (HP:0000533); CFP (HGNC:1777) —DISRUPTS→ Complement system activation (GO:0006955); Complement system activation (GO:0006955) —LEADS_TO→ Recurrent bacterial infections (HP:0002710). Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in CFP disrupt the complement system, specifically the alternative pathway, leading to increased susceptibility to infections.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that ADAMTSL4 and CFP do not converge on any shared downstream pathways or processes involved in maintaining connective tissue integrity or immune cell function, or that mutations in ADAMTSL4 do not affect complement system components, and vice versa. _(variant: Presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in gnomAD in the coding regions of ADAMTSL4 or CFP that do not segregate with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the interplay between extracellular matrix integrity and complement system function could reveal novel therapeutic targets for improving ocular health and immune defense, potentially through modulating matrix assembly or complement regulation.

#### 5. lymphatic malformation 13  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.378)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5083635, Reactome:R-HSA-5173214)

**Proposed mechanism:** THSD1 (HGNC:24124) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular Matrix Assembly and Organization (REACT:R-HSA-168772); Extracellular Matrix Assembly and Organization (REACT:R-HSA-168772) —LEADS_TO→ Ectopia lentis (HP:0001692); Extracellular Matrix Assembly and Organization (REACT:R-HSA-168772) —LEADS_TO→ Lymphatic malformation (HP:0030125); ADAMTSL4 (HGNC:29771) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular Matrix Assembly and Organization (REACT:R-HSA-168772). Loss-of-function mutations in THSD1 disrupt the normal assembly and organization of the extracellular matrix (ECM). This disruption affects the structural integrity of the lens zonules, leading to ectopia lentis. Concurrently, compromised ECM organization impacts lymphatic endothelial cell function and lymphatic vessel development, resulting in lymphatic malformations. While THSD1 is the primary focus for both diseases, ADAMTSL4, also implicated in ectopia lentis, is known to influence ECM processes, potentially converging on similar downstream pathways related to matrix integrity.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in THSD1 associated with ectopia lentis 2 with a clear loss-of-function mechanism (e.g., frameshift, nonsense mutations) that are absent or extremely rare in control populations (e.g., gnomAD frequency < 0.01%), while similar pathogenic variants are found in individuals with lymphatic malformation 13. _(variant: Any common variant (AF > 0.01) in THSD1 showing a statistically significant enrichment in cases vs controls for either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of THSD1 in extracellular matrix integrity could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting ECM homeostasis for both ocular and lymphatic vascular disorders. For instance, therapies aimed at stabilizing or enhancing ECM components might offer benefit.

#### 9. congenital thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.376)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5083635, Reactome:R-HSA-5173214)

**Proposed mechanism:** ADAMTSL4 (HGNC:25952) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Ectopia lentis (HP:0001741); ADAMTS13 (HGNC:230) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombocytopenia (HP:0001874); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (HP:0001898). Mutations in ADAMTSL4 disrupt extracellular matrix organization leading to ectopia lentis. Similarly, mutations in ADAMTS13, which also plays a role in extracellular matrix homeostasis (specifically in regulating von Willebrand factor), disrupt this process, leading to microangiopathic hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia, hallmarks of TTP. The convergence is on the broader pathway of extracellular matrix organization, which is essential for both ocular lens integrity and vascular health.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic studies reveal that mutations in ADAMTSL4 and ADAMTS13 do not converge on shared molecular pathways related to extracellular matrix organization, or if specific functional assays demonstrate independent roles for these genes with no cross-talk in matrix regulation, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: The presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in gnomAD within the coding regions of ADAMTSL4 or ADAMTS13 that do not segregate with either disease would weaken the hypothesis.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of extracellular matrix regulation in these distinct diseases could reveal novel therapeutic targets. For instance, interventions aimed at restoring extracellular matrix integrity or modulating specific components could potentially benefit patients with either condition, or highlight contraindications for certain therapies.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on extracellular matrix integrity could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both ocular fragility and systemic connective tissue disorders. Modulating pathways involved in matrix deposition or cross-linking might offer a unified treatment approach.
